applies_why: The judge text treats Isaiah 7:14's wording and prophetic-application senses as leaving the point UNDERDETERMINED, which is the single-verse openness the rule governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.
room: The phrase "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand": one reading is that it forbids calling Isaiah 7:14 UNDERDETERMINED because its wording and prophetic-application senses are both standing; the other is that it does not apply if the judge is weighing the challenger's and defender's chains rather than the verse alone.
why: The judge made UNDERDETERMINED rest on the single verse's two aspects being answered separately, but the rule says such a verse is not open and both senses stand.
